name: team_pulse_ask
description: Call ONLY when the user explicitly directs Team Pulse to answer. `ask` is server-side ONLINE GENERATION: a Team Pulse LLM composes a bounded answer over current team data. BY DEFAULT PREFER THE READ TOOLS (team_pulse_info / team_pulse_search / team_pulse_get / team_pulse_resources) — read the corpus and compose the answer yourself: cheaper, full-fidelity data, and you are already an LLM that can synthesize from raw reads.

prompt.description: The question to ask Team Pulse.

focus.description: Optional lens resource id for orientation (e.g. 'projects/team-pulse').

name: team_pulse_configure
description: Call when the user gives their team-pulse endpoint URL: persists it for this user to ~/.amplifier/team-pulse/config.yaml (or $AMPLIFIER_TEAM_PULSE_DIR/config.yaml); the data tools then work immediately, no restart. client_id: optional, only to override the built-in default. This bundle prefers Azure AD (bearer) auth — already az login'd means the URL save is the entire setup, no key needed. It has no key parameter by design: a shared API key (automation/service scenarios where bearer isn't viable) goes in AMPLIFIER_TEAM_PULSE_KEY and beats az when both are present, so set one only if you specifically need it.

url.description: Team-pulse endpoint URL (must start with https://).

client_id.description: Azure AD application (client) ID (optional; used for az auth mode). Omit to use the built-in default.

name: team_pulse_download_corpus
description: Bulk-download the whole mined corpus (every sub-corpus the server exposes) to a LOCAL DIRECTORY — run your own agents / embeddings / grep over it offline. One zip fetch, extracted as a .md tree under dest_dir. Returns a SUMMARY {written, dest_dir, folder, bytes}, NOT the page bodies: pulling hundreds of docs into context would crash the session. Offline BULK path only; in-session Q&A goes to team_pulse_search / team_pulse_get. Needs per-user BEARER (az) auth; a shared API key is refused (403), a bulk pull having to be attributable to a member. Optional folder narrows to ONE sub-corpus — names are instance-specific, so get them from team_pulse_info() (collections[].sub_corpora), never assume them.

dest_dir.description: Local directory to extract the corpus into (created if absent).

folder.description: Optional sub-corpus narrow — a sub-corpus id-prefix. Names vary per instance; get them from team_pulse_info() (collections[].sub_corpora). Omit for the whole corpus. An unknown name simply yields an empty result.

name: team_pulse_get
description: Fetch a single resource by full ID. Returns the resource envelope {id, title, type, data, metadata}. ID shape is '<type>/<slug>', e.g. 'members/jdoe' or 'questions/higher-level-work'. Available types are server-defined -- see team_pulse_info()'s resource_types. Returns a 404 envelope if unknown.

name: team_pulse_graph
description: Use for cross-resource relationships (who's on what, which projects roll up to which initiative): the full composed entity graph — every resource of every type plus computed reverse edges — in one response. Large payload; prefer team_pulse_resources / team_pulse_get for targeted lookups.

name: team_pulse_info
description: Discover what the API exposes: the SERVER's self-description -- API name/version, the auth scheme it documents, capabilities, endpoint catalog, content collections. Remote; needs network + working auth. It is the server's view of itself, NOT which URL you are pointed at or how you authenticated -- that is team_pulse_status.

name: team_pulse_prefix
description: List resources whose ID starts with the given path prefix. Example: prefix='projects' returns all projects. Cheaper and more precise than team_pulse_search for hierarchical lookups.

name: team_pulse_resources
description: List team-pulse resources -> the list envelope {resources: [{id, title, type}], count}. `type` narrows to one resource class; valid types are server-defined and vary by deployment -- check team_pulse_info()'s resource_types for the current live set first (unsupported type -> HTTP 400). `status` (active | archived | all) picks lifecycle state for type=question; default active hides archived. `collection` lists a content-collection folder.

type.description: Optional resource type filter. Valid values are server-specific -- check team_pulse_info()'s resource_types before assuming a type exists.

status.description: Lifecycle filter; applies ONLY to type=question (silently ignored for other types). 'active' (default) hides archived questions; 'archived' returns only archived; 'all' returns both. Invalid values -> 400.

name: team_pulse_search
description: Naive text search across all team-pulse resources. Returns the same list envelope as team_pulse_resources. Default limit 50, max 200. Search is substring-matchy — for precise lookups by ID prefer team_pulse_get or team_pulse_prefix.

name: team_pulse_status
description: Diagnose auth/connection failures — 'which server am I talking to, how am I authenticating?' — even when auth is broken or the server is unreachable. Reports THIS client's locally-resolved config; no network call, no secrets: base_url (the team-pulse endpoint you point at), auth_mode ('key' | 'az'), credential_type, api_app_id, forced, resolved, az_identity_hint (raw Azure AD token claim, e.g. upn -- decoded client-side, signature NOT verified, None in key mode). That hint is NOT team-pulse's resolved identity and may not match it; team_pulse_whoami gives the server-verified team member record (handle/member_id), team_pulse_info the SERVER's documented capabilities and endpoints.

name: team_pulse_submit_answer
description:
Submit a session-mined answer to a team-pulse reflection question -- an AI-generated answer attributed to a specific user, synthesized from their Context Intelligence sessions.

question_id: the BARE SLUG (e.g. 'higher-level-work'), NOT hierarchical 'questions/<slug>' — strip that prefix; get valid slugs from team_pulse_resources(type='question'), using data.id (or strip the prefix off the list-envelope id). user_id: the github username of the person the answer is about; the bundle records it as a github-namespaced identity, and the API stores it verbatim, resolving to a team member at read time. generated_at: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the answer was generated. metadata: optional opaque bag — session provenance (source_session_ids), timing, and any other context live INSIDE it.

question_id.description: Bare question slug (e.g. 'higher-level-work'). Hierarchical 'questions/<slug>' is rejected.

user_id.description: GitHub username of the person the answer is about.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the answer was generated.

metadata.description: Optional opaque bag stored verbatim by the server. Session provenance lives here as source_session_ids (array of Context Intelligence session IDs); may also carry timing, model, confidence, etc.

name: team_pulse_whoami
description: Resolve the caller's identity -- for 'me' / 'my' / 'mine' requests ('my projects', 'my record', 'what am I assigned'). Takes no input. Returns how the caller authenticated and whether a per-user identity is available: the SERVER-verified team-pulse identity (handle/member_id), unlike team_pulse_status()'s az_identity_hint -- a raw, unverified Azure token claim that may not match.
